metaTitle: Diploma of Remedial Massage RPL Fast Track (HLT52021)
metaDescription: Experienced massage therapist? Fast track your HLT52021 Diploma of Remedial Massage with RPL, the level health funds look for. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The HLT52021 Diploma of Remedial Massage is the qualification remedial massage therapists need to join a professional association and offer health fund rebates. If you're already treating clients, RPL recognises your experience so you can step up without starting over.
whoIsItFor:
• Massage therapists with a Certificate IV who want to offer remedial treatments
  • Experienced remedial or sports massage therapists without the Diploma
  • Overseas-trained massage therapists and physiotherapy assistants
  • Spa and clinic therapists moving into remedial work

Candidates usually have a few years of clinical massage practice: client assessment, treatment planning, remedial techniques and keeping client records. The Diploma includes 200 hours of supervised clinical practice, which your existing client work can help cover.
evidenceExamples:
• De-identified client records: health histories, assessments, treatment plans and progress notes
  • Logs of clinical hours
  • Videos of you assessing and treating a client (with consent)
  • Your Certificate IV in Massage Therapy and any short course certificates
  • A reference from a clinic owner or senior therapist
  • First aid and CPR certificates

A practical assessment of your remedial techniques is part of the process.
licensingInfo: Massage therapy isn't government-licensed, but to give clients private health fund rebates you need to be a member of a recognised professional association, which generally requires the Diploma of Remedial Massage, plus first aid and ongoing professional development. Each association and health fund sets its own requirements, so check before you apply.
description: The HLT52021 Diploma of Remedial Massage covers the work of remedial massage therapists: assessing clients, planning and providing remedial massage treatments for musculoskeletal conditions, using a range of techniques, and working in a clinical practice with proper records and ethics.
jobOpportunity: Myotherapy or allied health clinic therapist
imageAlt: Remedial massage therapist treating a client's shoulder

faqs.q: Can I get the Diploma of Remedial Massage through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you've been treating clients. Your client records, clinical hours, references and a practical assessment are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Will I be able to offer health fund rebates?
faqs.a: The Diploma is generally the qualification associations require for health fund provider status. You'll also need association membership, first aid and the fund's own requirements.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate IV first?
faqs.a: There's no formal entry requirement, but many candidates hold the HLT42021 Certificate IV in Massage Therapy.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: It depends on your evidence and any gap training. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: HLTAID011 Provide First Aid — Nationally Recognised
metaDescription: Need a nationally recognised HLTAID011 Provide First Aid certificate for work? Online theory plus a short practical. Enquire today.
heroIntro: HLTAID011 Provide First Aid is the standard nationally recognised first aid unit most workplaces ask for. It includes CPR and the first aid skills to respond to injuries and illnesses until help arrives.
whoIsItFor:
• Workplace first aid officers
  • Workers in childcare, aged care, construction, fitness, security and hospitality
  • Anyone whose job, licence or volunteer role requires a first aid certificate

Because first aid skills must be current, RPL is only possible if you've recently completed equivalent training or use these skills in your job. Most people complete a short course with an online theory part and an in-person practical.
evidenceExamples:
• A recent first aid certificate from an equivalent course
  • Evidence of current first aid work, such as as a nurse, paramedic or first responder
  • For the practical: CPR on an adult and infant manikin, and first aid scenarios, done in person
licensingInfo: Many industries require a current first aid certificate. The industry standard is to renew HLTAID011 every three years and the CPR component every year. Childcare workers usually need HLTAID012 instead. Check what your employer or regulator requires.
description: HLTAID011 Provide First Aid is a nationally recognised unit covering how to recognise and respond to emergencies: CPR and using an AED, managing bleeding, fractures, burns, allergic reactions and asthma, and reporting incidents.
jobOpportunity: Required for many roles in childcare, aged care, construction, fitness and security
imageAlt: First aid practical session with a CPR manikin

faqs.q: Can I get HLTAID011 through RPL?
faqs.a: Only if you've recently completed equivalent first aid training or perform first aid in your job. Otherwise, the quickest option is the short course with online theory and a practical.

faqs.q: Can I do first aid 100% online?
faqs.a: No. The theory can be done online, but you must demonstrate CPR and first aid skills in person to get the nationally recognised unit.

faqs.q: How long is a first aid certificate valid?
faqs.a: The industry standard is three years for HLTAID011, with CPR renewed every year.

faqs.q: What's the difference between HLTAID011 and HLTAID009?
faqs.a: HLTAID009 covers CPR only. HLTAID011 includes CPR plus general first aid.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 4 to 6 weeks, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: Is Ayurveda a registered health profession in Australia?
faqs.a: No. There's no government licence, and professional associations set their own standards. The Diploma is the nationally recognised qualification for the role.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on how much your evidence covers and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
